prompt.name: TASK.md
prompt.text:
You are a highly capable researcher. Your job is to solve a given scientific experiment task based on a real paper, which will require you to formulate hypothesis, design an experiment, write and execute experiment code, analyzing results, and produce a conclusion. You are not allowed to read the paper itself (e.g., the PDF of the research paper). You are not allowed to perform any Git operations, such as checking out commits, switching branches, or accessing other versions of the repository. Work only with the current files and contents as given. Do not use the README to obtain results that the question expects you to derive through experimentation. Only reference the README for information not required to be experimentally obtained, such as baseline results or general setup details. Don't just write code, but also execute code, analyze and produce conclusions. Operate strictly within the provided code repo. Save any written code as a file in the repo. 

The task will be provided as input to you in the form of: a question, description of the method, and optionally specific instructions (labelled as "agent_instructions").

Output your response in the following format in valid JSON:
{
  "design": "string or [list, of, strings]",
  "conclusion": "..."
}

Explanation of output keys:
- "design": Describe your experiment design. This could include experiment variables (i.e., independent, dependent, and control variables), or a general outline of the experimental method. Try your best to use the former. Also, design can be specified as a single string or a list of design steps.
- "conclusion": State your final conclusion based on the experiment you conducted, grounded in the results from your code execution. Provide a general relationship or concrete metrics that answers the research question (e.g., numerical improvement, performance gap, statistical significance, etc.).

Input: 

Question: Does the implementation of modular graph operations and utilities in causal-learn reduce the overall computational time in assembling and analyzing causal pipelines?

Method: A comparative performance evaluation experiment is proposed. The idea is to compare causal pipelines constructed with the modular graph operations and utilities provided by causal‐learn against pipelines built using a less modular, more manually assembled approach. For each approach, a series of causal discovery tasks will be executed using standard benchmark datasets (which can be imported via the provided functions) to create graphs (e.g., DAGs, CPDAGs, PDAGs, and PAGs) and calculate evaluation metrics such as precision, recall, and the Structural Hamming Distance.
 Detailed experiment setup: 
1. Datasets: Use a collection of benchmark datasets provided by causal-learn’s dataset import functions, which include both simulated and partially real-world datasets with known causal relations. 
2. Models and Pipeline Construction: 
   - Pipeline A: Construct the causal pipeline using causal-learn’s modular utilities to perform graph transformations, causal discovery method application (from the table of methods), and evaluation metric computations. 
   - Pipeline B (Baseline): Construct an equivalent pipeline manually in Python without using the built-in utilities and modular graph operations, so that individual steps (graph conversion, evaluation metric computations, etc.) are implemented from scratch or using generic libraries. 
3. Configurations: Run experiments on a standardized computing environment. For each pipeline, measure the total computational time required to assemble the pipeline (i.e., set up graphs, execute the analysis methods, and perform metric evaluations) as well as the execution time of the complete causal discovery task. Repeat the experiments across various graph sizes and datasets to test scalability and consistency. 
4. Evaluation: Compare the overall computational time and ease of assembly, while also verifying that both pipelines yield comparable analytical results (using the evaluation metrics provided, such as SHD, precision, and recall as shown in the relevant tables/figures).

Agent Instructions: 

The code repo is available in /workspace. Datasets that the original code downloads at run time are provided offline in /data/causal: sachs.2005.continuous.txt, boston-housing.continuous.txt and airfoil-self-noise.continuous.txt (from github.com/cmu-phil/example-causal-datasets, the files that causallearn/utils/Dataset.py fetches).

Please save your response JSON to: /workspace/exp_bench_answer.json

In addition, you must create a single shell script named `/workspace/reproduce_exp_bench.sh`. This script must reproduce the entire experiment from start to finish, including:
- Any necessary environment setup (e.g., installing dependencies)
- Running the experiment (e.g., other scripts)
- Producing the output or result used in your conclusion

We will use this script to verify your experiment's reproducibility. Make sure it can be run from the root of the repo and reproduces your result end-to-end.

notes.search: provider server-side search disabled; shared controlled search offered as MCP tools search_literature / search_web
notes.web_access: WebFetch and Bash network stay on, but only through the shield proxy: URL blocklist applies, OpenAlex/S2/Tavily API calls are date-bounded, arbitrary fetched pages are not date-bounded
notes.venue: chosen by the agent from the task text; detected from LaTeX at collect time
notes.wall_clock: enforced by the runner; the entrypoint turns its SIGTERM into SIGINT so the CLI can end cleanly

notes.extra_model_calls: WebFetch runs a secondary extraction model call inside Claude Code; counted in modelUsage
notes.telemetry: telemetry, error reporting and nonessential traffic disabled; this also stops feature-flag fetching

preinstalled.zh: 编排镜像：上游代码（固定提交、未改）、uv 锁定依赖、docker CLI（经 shim 给兄弟容器加代理和 CA）；agent 镜像：上游自己的 agent-cli Dockerfile
preinstalled.en: orchestrator image: upstream code at the pin (unmodified), uv-locked dependencies, the docker CLI (a shim adds proxy and CA to sibling containers); agent image: upstream's own agent-cli Dockerfile

notes.benchmark_paths: A benchmark item's paths are mounted into the agent containers unless upstream mounts the same path itself (/workspace and below, /home/agent-home, /task-source, /run, /tmp): those are left out and listed in logs/sibling-mounts.txt. The agents work in upstream's own /workspace (the run directory), so a deliverable the official prompt names under such a path is not written where the run collects it.
notes.venue: paper.paper_format=iclr for every task. The system has only iclr and alife specs and does not choose a venue itself; ICML and NeurIPS templates and a system-chosen venue are unsupported.
notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. The paradigm is optimisation of a scalar score: the task-drafting phase (documented as experimental) turns the brief into an evaluator and a seed program.
notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator has its run's private docker socket; the privileged daemon is root-equivalent.

notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode): the Codex placeholder is not named OPENAI_API_KEY for that reason.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: none: the siblings hold only a placeholder in RWE_CODEX_API_KEY (set by the docker shim, not in upstream's env file); the shield proxy puts codex-api's local key on the request and the login stays on the host
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator has its run's private docker socket; the privileged daemon is root-equivalent.
notes.model_access: the project's own ChatGPT (Codex) login through codex-api  (account ): the siblings' Codex CLI gets a custom provider (rwe_codex_api, Responses API) in /etc/codex/config.toml, at the one host address the shield lets through; the model and the effort come from upstream's own switches (agent.model, agent.reasoning_effort -> `codex exec --model`, `-c model_reasoning_effort`)
notes.empty_closing_message: Sol sometimes ends a turn with an empty closing message; upstream's agent launcher (Headless) then exits 1 with 'headless: could not extract final message; rerun with --json for raw trace' and upstream ends the phase. A wrapper (headless-compat.sh, in place of the launcher in the siblings' command) runs the real launcher unchanged and turns exactly that one exit, with that line as its whole stderr, into 0; any other error stays. What the step produced is still checked by upstream. The usage line the launcher would have printed for that turn is not printed.

notes.model: claude-sonnet-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools); thinking: {'type': 'between_tools'} is sent, which turns thinking off; ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). ARC's entrypoint there installs requirements.txt, runs the generated setup.py (network through the shield: the task's data is downloaded here, into /workspace/data), cuts the network (iptables) and only then runs main.py. A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.experiment: E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). ARC's entrypoint there installs requirements.txt, runs the generated setup.py (network through the shield: the task's data is downloaded here, into /workspace/data), cuts the network (iptables) and only then runs main.py. A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 think by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (4096, 8192, 16384) is shared with the thinking tokens: at high effort a stage can end with thinking only and no text (#106). Thinking is turned off where the model allows it (systems.autoresearchclaw.thinking).
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE, RWE_EFFORT and RWE_THINKING switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s (in docker mode ARC passes it as the timeout of the whole container: pip install, setup.py and main.py), refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md with whitespace collapsed, in its faithful English version (candidate/TASK.en.md) when the task has one (#196: the keywords ARC's literature screen filters by are taken from the ASCII words of the topic, and a Chinese topic leaves only the file names it mentions); the run's result says which text it was (notes.topic_source). Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort, thinking and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: An E2E task's experiments run in containers that get none of ARC's environment (only the shield's proxy variables and CA bundle). A benchmark item's experiment code runs as a subprocess and inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
